stories.title: Josh Hart discusses mental health struggles
stories.summary: Knicks forward Josh Hart told reporters this week that he is not in a good place mentally during the team's difficult start to the season. Hart stated he is struggling and does not know how to break out of it. The season remains ongoing.

stories.title: South Korean police face elevated mental health risks
stories.summary: A nationwide study indicates South Korean police officers who experience major trauma face significantly higher vulnerability to post-traumatic stress disorder, depression, and suicidal behavior compared to the general population. The research highlights a critical gap in occupational health data regarding specific law enforcement work functions.

stories.title: Kenyan study tracks youth suicidal distress
stories.summary: A clinical investigation at Kenyatta National Hospital suggests suicidal behavior among adolescents emerges gradually from cumulative life pressures rather than isolated crises. Researchers found that psychological strain develops over months or years, driven by the convergence of personal vulnerability, academic pressure, family discord, and structural disadvantages.

stories.title: Kazakhstan health ministry lists mental health warning signs
stories.summary: Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Health has published a guide on recognizing emotional burnout, anxiety, and insomnia. Officials advise seeking professional support when persistent low mood or changes in energy levels begin to interfere with daily life. The ministry aims to help residents identify when feelings require medical intervention.

stories.title: How a deadly shooting sparked a conversation about mold and mental health - The Washington Post
Meghalaya mental health policy proposed as tribal model
stories.summary: Rajya Sabha MP James K. Sangma suggested Meghalaya’s mental health policy could serve as a model for tribal youth migrating for work or education. The policy, approved in 2022, aims to address social determinants of mental ill-health and provide culturally sensitive care for those facing isolation.

stories.title: Prayagraj jails to offer weekly counselling
stories.summary: The state government will introduce weekly psychological counselling sessions for inmates in Prayagraj, Kaushambi, and Pratapgarh jails. Trained psychologists will provide two-hour sessions to address stress, anxiety, and loneliness. The initiative is expected to reach 3,500 inmates who are currently separated from their families and society.

stories.title: Student mental health challenges reach four-year high
stories.summary: A recent UnitedHealthcare survey reports that over 60 percent of college students experienced a mental or behavioral health concern in the past year. Rates of stress, anxiety, and depression among students have reached their highest levels in the survey's four-year history. Help is available via 988.

stories.title: Report Details Extreme Depression and Suicide Risks Facing Incarcerated Youth - Davis Vanguard
Review links late-life suicidality to multiple factors
stories.summary: An umbrella review of 423 studies suggests that suicidality in adults aged 50 and older is linked to depression, pain, and loneliness. Researchers concluded that these outcomes cannot be explained by psychiatric disorders alone, as they reflect a complex synthesis of various risk and protective factors.

stories.title: Healthcare workers report widespread workplace bullying
stories.summary: More than half of healthcare workers in a hospital setting experienced workplace bullying, according to new research. Despite the psychological and occupational burdens noted by the study, nearly three-quarters of those affected never reported the mistreatment to their institution. Silence remains the primary response to interpersonal hostility.

stories.title: Media responsibility in mental health reporting
stories.summary: Dr. Muzaffar Husain Ghazali argues that media outlets carry a significant responsibility when reporting on mental health and suicide. The author notes that while irresponsible coverage can deepen despair for those in distress, balanced and hopeful reporting can potentially save lives through careful presentation.

stories.title: Forest bathing as a public health measure
stories.summary: Japan introduced the practice of forest bathing in 1982 as a public health measure to combat work-related stress and rapid urbanization. The activity focuses on using senses to experience the forest environment rather than traditional exercise. It is intended as a mindfulness-based break from daily life.

stories.title: Guide released for choosing meditation apps
stories.summary: Mashable has released a guide for selecting meditation apps based on user personality and preferences. The publication notes that a lack of clear feature information on app websites can pressure consumers into free trials or cause them to abandon their search for a suitable mindfulness tool entirely.

stories.title: MasterClass offers mindfulness instruction
stories.summary: The online service MasterClass is marketing a mindfulness course featuring Jon Kabat-Zinn. The platform relies on the proposition that celebrity instructors increase learner attention. The service delivers slimmed-down instruction via direct-to-camera talks, aiming to provide an accessible introduction to mindfulness practice for its subscribers.

stories.title: Pianist to host live meditation event
stories.summary: Pianist Chad Lawson will perform selections from his new album, hush, at a live meditation event in West Hollywood on November 16. The evening, presented by The DEN Meditation, will combine piano performance with guided loving-kindness meditation to celebrate the launch of Meditation Magazine's latest issue.

stories.title: Mindfulness program shows preliminary well-being gains
stories.summary: A community-based trial in Seoul evaluated an eight-week Mindfulness-based Vitality Promotion curriculum. The study reported high participant acceptability and preliminary improvements in psychological and physical well-being. Researchers assessed the program using standardized quantitative self-report questionnaires administered before and after the curriculum was completed by participants.

stories.title: Study links insomnia to major health risks
stories.summary: A study published in Sleep Medicine Reviews analyzed 20 review studies and found insomnia linked to a 26 percent increased risk of stroke. The research also associated insomnia with higher risks of dementia and mental health conditions, though authors noted the findings do not prove direct causation.

stories.title: The clinical use of music for healing
stories.summary: Music therapy is a structured, evidence-based healthcare profession using music to support physical and emotional wellbeing. Unlike listening to a playlist, it involves a purposeful therapeutic relationship with clear goals and assessment. Music activates multiple brain areas simultaneously, including those linked to memory, movement, and language.

stories.title: Routine linked to lower pain and depression
stories.summary: University of Missouri researchers found that older adults with consistent daily schedules reported less physical pain and fewer symptoms of depression. Keeping regular times for sleeping and eating may help regulate the body's internal clock, which influences mood and overall health. Consistency is now a health strategy.

stories.title: Brain stimulation study finds sham works as well as real
stories.summary: Adults with depression who used a home brain stimulation kit for six weeks reported improvements. However, participants using a switched-off sham device with a decoy game reported identical results. The study suggests the intervention is effective, regardless of whether the device is actually functioning.

stories.title: Inconsistent sleep timing linked to cardiovascular risk
stories.summary: Preliminary research analyzing over one million nights of sleep suggests that irregular bedtimes and varying sleep durations are linked to an elevated risk of heart attack and stroke. Shifts in sleep timing over six months corresponded with a 20% to 23% greater risk of serious cardiovascular events.

stories.title: Older women face higher risk of short sleep
stories.summary: A study of 9,590 adults aged 65 and older in China found that women face a higher relative risk of short sleep duration than men. Researchers at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital noted that abnormal sleep durations affected nearly forty-five percent of the surveyed population overall.

stories.title: Sleep apnoea linked to dementia and weight gain
stories.summary: Sleep apnoea is associated with a 33% higher risk of dementia and a 45% higher risk of Alzheimer’s disease, according to a Greek sleep specialist. The condition, which affects an estimated 75% of people with obesity, can also impair memory and concentration. Symptoms include loud snoring.

stories.title: Metabolic syndrome linked to poorer sleep
stories.summary: A study of adult inpatients found that metabolic syndrome is significantly associated with poorer sleep continuity and more frequent nocturnal arousals. Researchers examined objective sleep architecture to clarify the relationship between metabolic health and sleep efficiency, which had remained unclear in prior investigations.

stories.title: Bedroom heat reduces sleep quality
stories.summary: A study of older adults found that sleep efficiency decreases by 5 to 10% when bedroom temperatures rise from 25 to 30 degrees Celsius. The 18-month study observed that elevated air temperatures impair the quality of rest and reduce the duration of deep sleep.

stories.title: Sleep lab finds split on snooze button effects
stories.summary: A Stockholm University study found that regular snoozers performed better on thinking tests after repeated alarms, despite not feeling more awake. While participants did not report feeling more alert, the repeated alarms appeared to influence cognitive performance compared to waking up immediately.

stories.title: Wearables may track sleep and mental health
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of California, San Francisco and San Diego found that irregular sleep-wake schedules are linked to more severe symptoms of depression and anxiety. Wearable devices are increasingly used to track sleep stages, offering potential new clues about a user's mental health.

stories.title: Cannabis use linked to poorer sleep quality
stories.summary: A study of 1,266 people found that lifetime cannabis use is associated with poorer objective sleep quality, even when participants did not report feeling worse. Researchers tracked participants for 35 years, comparing wrist-monitor sleep data with self-reported assessments. Subjective perception and objective data remain at odds.

stories.title: Marijuana use as sleep aid questioned
stories.summary: A Northwestern Medicine study of 1,266 participants found that cannabis users objectively had worse sleep quality despite not reporting it. Scientists tracked usage over 35 years, concluding that marijuana may be making sleep quality worse even as it is widely used as a sleep aid.

stories.title: Productivity and the biological clock
stories.summary: Hanan Badie of the Al Jasra Cultural and Social Club argues that professional pressure to wake up early may conflict with natural human physiology. She suggests that the traditional early-morning workday might contribute to chronic fatigue and poor concentration rather than serving as a sign of discipline.

stories.title: Compression socks market shifts to wellness
stories.summary: The global market for compression socks is moving from niche medical use to a consumer wellness category. According to an IndexBox report, demand is now bifurcating into performance-oriented recovery gear and wellness products focused on daily comfort and preventative care.

stories.title: Strength training improves function after 60
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 41 trials involving 3,141 participants aged 60 or older found that resistance training improves specific strength relative to muscle mass. The study suggests that muscle size is not the only factor in maintaining the ability to perform everyday tasks like climbing stairs.

stories.title: Olympian says competitive streak is unhealthy
stories.summary: Five-time world champion rower Alex Gregory claims that his Olympic training was not healthy for his back, heart, or head. At 42, he attributes his fitness to dialing back his competitive streak, suggesting that the intensity required for elite sports is not sustainable for long-term health.

stories.title: Hip health habits for mobility
stories.summary: Maintaining independence as you age can start with simple exercises at home, according to mobility advocates. Experts suggest that incorporating small, accessible hip movements into an everyday routine can help keep individuals stable and steady as they age.

stories.title: Strength training for the over-50s
stories.summary: Personal trainer Edwina Jenner says strength training is essential for metabolic and heart health during perimenopause. Jenner, who previously focused on cardio for two decades, now advocates for dumbbells to safeguard against osteoporosis. The transition from cardio bunny to weightlifter is presented as a transformative health strategy.

stories.title: Mel Robbins adopts resistance training
stories.summary: Mel Robbins, 58, has added strength training to her routine after consulting with medical experts. Robbins says she previously avoided weights due to a fear of bulking up, a concern she now describes as a joke. She aims to maintain her mobility into her late 90s.

stories.title: Strength exercises for stair climbing
stories.summary: Osteopath Ales Ulishchenko says climbing stairs is essentially a repeated single-leg squat. Maintaining independence as one ages requires strong quads, glutes, and calves, alongside the balance needed to stand on one leg. The focus remains on the mechanics of moving up and down steps safely.

stories.title: Wall exercises for core strength
stories.summary: As the focus of core strength shifts from aesthetics to daily functionality, experts suggest using a wall for support. Wall planks and sits are proposed as equipment-free ways to build the muscles needed for everyday tasks like carrying groceries or standing from a chair without gym costs.

stories.title: Increasing walking intensity for longevity
stories.summary: Orthopedic surgeon Dr. Vonda Wright says walking is a low-impact way to improve fitness and boost longevity. For those who find standard walking too easy, Wright suggests increasing intensity to dial up the benefits. The activity remains free, accessible, and capable of being performed almost anywhere.

stories.title: Building strength in midlife
stories.summary: After decades of prioritizing parenting over exercise, one woman began strength training at 55 to regain physical capability. She credits her renewed health to a willingness to try new activities, noting that her relationship with fitness changed significantly once she committed to the process in midlife.

stories.title: Ultra-processed foods and heart failure risk
stories.summary: A study of 6,531 US adults published in JACC: Heart Failure links each additional daily serving of ultra-processed food to a 5% higher relative risk of heart failure. The classification includes industrial formulations like packaged cookies and ready meals, though it does not measure specific nutritional value.

stories.title: Plant-based diet and runner body fat
stories.summary: An exploratory study of seven male endurance runners found that a short-term transition to a plant-based diet was associated with reduced body fat while maintaining fat-free mass. The research tracked inflammatory and vascular biomarkers during sequential dietary phases to assess the impact on performance and body composition.

stories.title: Kashmiri wazwan and diabetes prevalence
stories.summary: Experts say the traditional Kashmiri wazwan, which can contain up to 5,500 calories per meal, is a key factor in rising diabetes cases. The multi-course feast is a staple of local social life, often exceeding the average daily caloric requirement in a single sitting.

stories.title: Peanut intake and brain function
stories.summary: A study of 31 healthy adults aged 60 to 75 found that consuming 60 grammes of unsalted peanuts daily for 16 weeks improved insulin responsiveness in brain regions linked to memory. Researchers suggest regular consumption may support cognitive function, though the mechanism remains under investigation.

stories.title: Lemon tops CDC nutrient density ranking
stories.summary: A CDC study ranking nutrient-dense produce placed lemon at the top of familiar fruits with a score of 18.72, ahead of strawberries and oranges. Blueberries did not meet the study cutoff for the list, which measures the concentration of 17 nutrients relative to calorie content.

stories.title: New fibre supplement for IBS
stories.summary: Scientists at Edith Cowan University have developed a fibre supplement called ur gut, which combines resistant starch and psyllium husk. The formulation aims to support gut bacteria and stabilize IBS symptoms like bloating and abdominal pain without the digestive discomfort often associated with traditional fibre intake.

stories.title: Ayurvedic perspective on diabetes
stories.summary: Dr. Sayali Devkate says common dietary myths often lead to unnecessary restrictions for diabetic patients. The discussion highlights the importance of separating misconceptions from medical facts, advocating for an Ayurvedic approach to management that focuses on preventive measures and informed lifestyle choices.

stories.title: Plant-forward diets and health outcomes
stories.summary: New research suggests a plant-forward eating pattern is associated with a lower body mass index and reduced odds of obesity and diabetes. The study indicates that a diet rich in minimally processed plant foods may offer health benefits without requiring a strictly meat-free regimen.

stories.title: The role of chewing in digestion
stories.summary: Dietitian Suhasini Viswanathan says digestion begins in the mouth and that rushing through meals can lead to discomfort. Proper chewing is described as an essential, often overlooked component of the digestive process that requires slowing down during mealtimes.

stories.title: Functional medicine doctor on longevity
stories.summary: Florida physician Dr. Mitch Ghen says he eats coffee, cacao, and raw honey daily to support healthy aging. Ghen, who has practiced functional medicine for 45 years, notes that these foods make a massive difference, though he acknowledges that sustainable habits matter more than any single superfood.

stories.title: Longevity advice from a Florida physician
stories.summary: Dr. Mitch Ghen says he consumes coffee, cacao, and raw honey to support healthy aging. He considers three to four cups of organic coffee a day to be a sweet spot for longevity, while emphasizing that overall dietary sustainability is more important than relying on specific foods.

stories.title: Daily dietary choices for aging
stories.summary: Dr. Mitch Ghen, a functional medicine physician, says he consumes coffee, cacao, and raw honey daily to support long-term health. Ghen incorporates these into his routine, starting his mornings with coffee mixed with cacao, and notes their potential contribution to overall health.

stories.title: Dietary advice for longevity
stories.summary: Dr. Linda Shiue suggests that improving diet and increasing physical activity are key to living a longer life. While many seek a magic formula for aging, experts note that no single food serves as a simple solution for extending one's lifespan.

stories.title: 4 Emerging Longevity Supplements Your Patients May Be Talking About - Verywell Health
Super Age Games tests physical and cognitive fitness
stories.summary: The inaugural Super Age Games in New York City invited 500 amateur athletes to complete eight trials measuring agility, balance, and aerobic fitness. Participants ranged from their 20s to their 80s, with the event aiming to provide a metric for how well individuals are aging.

stories.title: Acupuncture and moxibustion studied for post-stroke recovery
stories.summary: A systematic review of 47 randomized controlled trials involving 3,680 participants suggests that combined acupuncture and moxibustion may improve cognitive performance after a stroke. The study evaluated 15 different interventions, noting that post-stroke impairment often limits functional restoration and quality of life for patients.

stories.title: Yoga as a contribution to global wellness
stories.summary: Yoga is described as a significant global contribution of Bharatiya philosophical tradition, intended to foster harmony between individuals, society, and nature. The practice is framed as a journey beyond physical fitness, aiming to encourage self-discipline and the realization of inner potential for global welfare.

stories.title: Naturopathy Day 2026 to emphasize scientific research
stories.summary: The Ministry of Ayush will observe National Naturopathy Day on November 18, 2026, with a focus on evidence-informed approaches to preventive healthcare. The event aims to strengthen the scientific foundation of naturopathy through discussions on diet, physical activity, and stress management.

stories.title: Ayurvedic perspectives on diabetes management
stories.summary: With India hosting a large population of people living with diabetes, focus is shifting toward early detection and metabolic management. Ayurveda is being examined for its potential role in identifying warning signs and managing the progression of the condition before it reaches advanced stages.

stories.title: New wellness clinic opens in Poole
stories.summary: LaCure Longevity has opened a facility in Poole offering services ranging from reformer Pilates and infrared saunas to hyperbaric oxygen therapy. The clinic aims to provide a space where people can look after themselves, bringing various treatments together under one roof.

stories.title: Turkish hammam traditions arrive in Miami
stories.summary: Hürrem Hammam Wellness and Spa has opened a 20,000-square-foot facility in North Miami. Founder Gökhan Yavuzer states that the destination is designed to bring traditional Turkish hammam practices to a modern setting, focusing on atmosphere and the time taken to slow down.

stories.title: Sangam Healing Center launches integrated medicine approach
stories.summary: The Sangam Healing Center in Lakewood, Colorado, is combining traditional healing wisdom with Ayurveda and contemporary mental health perspectives. The center aims to create a holistic environment for personal transformation, utilizing Colorado's existing natural medicine framework to support its integrative approach.

stories.title: Aayush Wellness expands into shilajit market
stories.summary: Aayush Wellness Ltd has launched Himalayan Shilajit Drops to target consumer demand for energy and vitality supplements. The company is entering a market valued at $206.64 million in 2025, which is projected to reach $436.72 million by 2034.
